OmaStats 1.1 adds multi-GPU monitoring, a dedicated GPU panel, and a bundled ARM64 sampler.

- Each detected GPU has its own utilization history and bar readout. Settings lets you choose which cards appear in the bar, while the GPU tab keeps all cards available.
- The GPU tab shows utilization, memory, temperature, clock, power and fan readings where the hardware provides them.
- GPU identities use PCI addresses, including systems with multiple NVIDIA cards. The firmware boot display is the primary GPU, followed by other cards in PCI address order.
- Missing utilization readings are shown as unavailable. Intel cards show their clock when the driver does not expose utilization; i915 utilization collection remains unsupported.
- ARM64 Linux now gets a bundled static Rust sampler selected automatically at startup. Python remains the fallback for unsupported architectures or unusable binaries.
- Existing saved panel settings retain access to GPU details on upgrade. Stale GPU selections and missing NVIDIA telemetry helpers no longer hide or select the wrong cards.

Both bundled binaries are rebuilt twice in CI, compared byte-for-byte with the committed executables, and covered by checksums and GitHub build attestations. ARM64 CI also runs the bundled binary natively.

The full plugin archive includes both bundled architectures. Separate native sampler archives and DEB/RPM packages are provided for x86-64 and ARM64. The normal plugin installation remains:

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omastats.git --enable
```

Thanks to @Mr-Benedict for the multi-GPU support and dedicated GPU tab in #1 and #2. Tested on an RTX 3090 plus AMD integrated Radeon Graphics, including independent utilization changes under GPU load.
